structured_output.summary:
The big picture: the large-seed instrument (E113 onward) is sound, but the tree has not caught up with what it found. Two 100-seed results, E121 (early updates add nothing) and E126 (removing late updates costs -0.18 pp), contradict the global refutation of H10 and the retirement of H11/H11.2. Together they show late full-resolution samples and updates bind, while marginal early steps are worthless. That asymmetry has no Lvl1 hypothesis, even though it predicts several untested time levers: bs 2048 early, a 16 px trim, and bs 768 late, which was retired for a reason that no longer holds.

Several statuses are stale:
- H2 and H2.11 still list the bs-1536 revert as a lever (E126 refuted it) and call the 32 px trim rate unmeasured (E128 measured it at ~0.05 pp per 1%).
- H2.11.6, H2.20.4 and H2.20.5 are still 'open' despite decisive refutations.
- H2.10.6 is still 'open' even though E128 supports it.

The E127 depth-cut dismissal used the wrong slope, 0.5 pp/epoch instead of the measured ~1 pp/epoch. Two other cuts were never accuracy-tested: 3/3/2 and group-3 width 512.

The levers measured below the yardstick (the 85% freeze, possibly 2/3/3) imply a funded combination strategy, and nobody has built it. The 75% freeze point is unmeasured.

Gate bookkeeping is wrong in places:
- H4 miscounts the passing scored rows: E119 and E128 both pass.
- E123's provenance is unresolved.
- The 0.7518 acceptance floor looks tailored to E116's 0.7521.
- The banked 4.262 s comes from a recipe that passes the local gate about 27% of the time.

Finally, about eight 'free' tip components were adopted on 1-1.5 SE evidence. 100-seed removal ablations could recover margin at zero time, and lookahead removal would also save ~0.4%.
